components.question_it_answers: What did this trade actually earn, and what may a fee be charged on?
components.source_of_truth: the settlement asset's post-minus-pre balance; never a reported total
refusals: a rolled-back trade has no priceable outcome (NotCommitted)
pricing in an asset the trade did not settle in (AssetMismatch)

components.enforcement_point: after the engine commits, before the first ledger movement

components.authorisation: the trader sets their own agreement; nobody else can
components.atomicity: fee distribution rides in the settlement's transaction
components.conservation: shares are basis points of the fee and sum to it exactly

acceptance_test.name: a_verified_profit_pays_the_agreed_split_out_of_the_traders_balance
proves: the flagship strategy compiles to canonical X3BC and runs on the production engine
it executes against real CanonicalLedger balances
profit and fees are recomputed from the receipt, not read from an event
an insufficient-profit outcome is rejected before any state change
trader, developer and protocol are paid per the agreement
a receipt is produced and recorded

open_limits: Savings Engine is not implemented; it needs a credible pre-execution benchmark before any fee can rest on it.
Automation declarations parse and validate but do not yet lower to X3BC, so an economic workflow cannot be submitted as an automation.
Atomic multi-VM trading is unchanged: the atomic kernel still restricts legs to X3-native operations.
Language syntax for strategy/constraints/profit_share is deliberately deferred until these runtime semantics are proven.
